question.prompt: Name a famous robot or artificial intelligence from a science-fiction film, TV series, or book.
question.criteria: Any named fictional robot, android, or computer AI appearing in a science-fiction film, TV series, or book counts; humans merely wearing robotic armor do not.

answers.evidence: R2-D2 is an astromech droid in Star Wars.
C-3PO is a protocol droid in Star Wars.
WALL-E is the waste-collecting robot at the center of Pixar's WALL-E.
HAL 9000 is the spacecraft computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey.
Optimus Prime is the robotic Autobot leader in Transformers films and television.
Data is an android Starfleet officer in Star Trek: The Next Generation.
Bender is a bending robot in Futurama.
BB-8 is a spherical astromech droid in Star Wars.
EVE is a robotic probe searching for plant life in WALL-E.
Marvin is a chronically gloomy robot in The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.
Bishop is an android who accompanies the Colonial Marines in Aliens.
Robby the Robot is a robot character introduced in Forbidden Planet.
Gort is the humanoid robot accompanying Klaatu in The Day the Earth Stood Still.
R. Daneel Olivaw is a humaniform robot in Isaac Asimov's fiction.
R. Giskard Reventlov is a robot with telepathic abilities in Isaac Asimov's Robot novels.
KITT is the artificial intelligence built into the car in Knight Rider.
The Iron Giant is the enormous alien robot in the animated film of the same name.
Skynet is the military artificial intelligence in the Terminator franchise.
Rosie is the robot housekeeper in The Jetsons.
K-2SO is a reprogrammed Imperial security droid in Rogue One.
Sonny is a distinctive NS-5 robot in the film I, Robot.
Kryten is a service mechanoid in the television series Red Dwarf.
Johnny 5 is the robot that becomes sentient in Short Circuit.
TARS is a robot accompanying the astronauts in Interstellar.
CASE is a robot assisting the space mission in Interstellar.

question.explanation: Science fiction features everything from helpful droids and robot companions to sentient computers. Answers can come from screen or literary science fiction, not just stories set in space.
